{{Quote|My ultimate goal is a peaceful resolution to this conflict, above all. But if such a resolution requires the creation of a military, as decreed by the Senate, then I will abide by the will of the Republic, a Republic that has stood strong for a thousand generations, that has enjoyed peace for a thousand years.|Supreme Chancellor Palpatine|<ref name="Vote Date" />}}
The '''Military Creation Act''' was a bill proposed in the [[Galactic Senate/Legends|Galactic Senate]] during the [[Separatist Crisis/Legends|Separatist Crisis]], in the years leading up to the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]]. Created in response to increasing secessions from the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]], the Act authorized the creation of an Army of the Republic, to aid the local security forces, [[Judicial/Legends|Judicials]], and [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] that made up the Republic's peacekeeping forces. The Act remained in limbo for two years until, on [[22 BBY/Legends|13]]:3:6, a vote was at last set for it two months hence. Over the following weeks, vociferous debate and intense campaigning ensued as Senators and many others sought to either advocate or oppose the measure.

A number of major events marked the course of the Military Creation Act's debate, including the closing of [[Corellia/Legends|Corellia's]] borders, protests from [[Chandrila/Legends|Chandrila]] to [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]], a plea from [[Supreme Chancellor/Legends|Supreme Chancellor]] [[Palpatine/Legends|Palpatine]] to Separatist leader [[Count/Legends|Count]] [[Dooku/Legends|Dooku]] for peace, and an outpouring of arguments, demonstrations, and endorsements. [[Senator/Legends|Senator]] [[Onaconda Farr/Legends|Onaconda Farr]] produced an allegorical play favoring the Act, while Senator [[Jollin Resbin]] secured the endorsement of [[Podracer/Legends|podracer]] [[Boles Roor/Legends|Boles Roor]]. [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] [[Depa Billaba/Legends|Depa Billaba]] and [[Sar Labooda/Legends|Sar Labooda]] joined the opposition as the planet [[Carida/Legends|Carida]], home to a prestigious military academy, supported the Act.

On the day of the vote, 5:16, leading member of the opposition [[Padmé Amidala/Legends|Padmé Amidala]] was [[Plot to assassinate Senator Amidala/Legends|attacked]] by an [[Assassin/Legends|assassin]]. In the wake of the attack, the vote was postponed and Amidala was sent offworld. Meanwhile, a [[Clone trooper/Legends|clone army]] was discovered on [[Kamino/Legends|Kamino]], and after it was learned that the Separatists were raising an army of their own, [[Junior Representative/Legends|Representative]] [[Jar Jar Binks/Legends|Jar Jar Binks]] called for emergency powers to be granted to Chancellor Palpatine so he could activate the clone army for Republic use. The motion was successful, and the new [[Grand Army of the Republic/Legends|Grand Army of the Republic]] went on to fight in the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]].

==Description==
The Military Creation Act authorized the formation of an Army of the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Republic]].<ref name="Vote Date" /> Chancellor Palpatine did not reveal the articles of the Act or the scope of the vote beforehand,<ref name="Youth">{{HoloNetNewsWeb|50|news/1344_6.html|Legislative Youth Program Role-Plays Vote}}</ref> but had it been put to a vote, it would likely have been a yes/no matter on the issue, according to [[HoloNet News/Legends|HoloNet News]]. If then passed by the [[Galactic Senate/Legends|Galactic Senate]], a commission of [[Senator/Legends|Senators]] would need to be established to determine resource allocation for the Republic's new military. Certain sector and planetary forces would be chosen to contribute to the Army, though which forces would be used was a matter for further discussion.<ref name="Vote Date" /> Military academies on worlds such as [[Carida/Legends|Carida]], [[Raithal/Legends|Raithal]], and [[Corulag/Legends|Corulag]] would serve to train the soldiers,<ref name="Carida" /> and the [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] were proposed by some as leaders of the eventual army.<ref name="Point" />

==History==
===Galactic change===
{{Quote|I will not let this Republic that has stood for a thousand years be split in two.|Supreme Chancellor Palpatine|<ref name="AOTC">{{Film|II}}</ref>}}
At the time of the [[Separatist Crisis/Legends|Separatist Crisis]], the Republic had enjoyed peace for a thousand years, with planetary security and sector forces, [[Judicial Forces/Legends|Judicial Forces]], and the [[Jedi Order/Legends|Jedi Order]] serving as its peacekeepers.<ref name="Vote Date" /><ref name="Point" /><ref name="NEC">''[[The New Essential Chronology]]''</ref> The [[Stark Hyperspace War/Legends|Stark Hyperspace War]] of [[44 BBY/Legends|44 BBY]], however, had led some to conclude that these peacekeeping forces were merely a stop-gap solution and a more unified military, led from [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]], was needed.<ref name="Point" /> In [[24 BBY/Legends|24 BBY]], former [[Jedi Master/Legends|Jedi Master]] [[Count/Legends|Count]] [[Dooku/Legends|Dooku]] reappeared on the galactic stage, decrying the Republic's corruption and preaching separatism. Dooku formed a new, secessionist government, the [[Confederacy of Independent Systems/Legends|Confederacy of Independent Systems]], and thousands of planets began to rally to him.<ref name="NEC" /> Rumors of a Military Creation Act began to circulate before the Act was announced, but [[Supreme Chancellor/Legends|Supreme Chancellor]] [[Palpatine/Legends|Palpatine]] refused to come out in favor of an army.<ref name="LOE">''[[Labyrinth of Evil]]''</ref> That year, the official Military Creation Act was at last proposed in response to the Separatist threat, allowing for the creation of an Army of the Republic to counter Separatist threats.<ref name="Vote Date" />

[[File:Palpatine_Sets_Army_Vote_Date.png|thumb|left|220px|Palpatine announces the vote date for the Military Creation Act.]]
However, this would not be resolved swiftly. Two years of bureaucratic stalemate began, with the Act going nowhere as more worlds joined the Separatist cause.<ref name="Vote Date" /><ref name="NEC" /> [[22 BBY/Legends|22 BBY]] arrived with no solution to the deadlock;<ref name="Vote Date" /> meanwhile, the issue itself pushed away other worlds, including [[Ando/Legends|Ando]], which was insulted by the Republic's own plan to militarize after the forced demilitarization of their world.<ref name="Ando">{{HoloNetNewsWeb|45|news/13228_1.html|Ando, Sy Myrth Secede}}</ref> On [[22 BBY/Legends|13]]:3:6, Chancellor Palpatine at last announced, in an address on the [[HoloNet/Legends|HoloNet]], a vote date for the Act: 5:16, two months later. This gap would give time for Senators to return to [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]], as well as poll their constituencies. Both support and opposition forces to the Act were relieved to see an end to the stalemate, though both cautioned the consequences of a wrong vote; Senator [[Tikkes/Legends|Tikkes]] was concerned of the time that additional discussions would take. Despite being publicly against the Act, Palpatine made no partisan comments during his announcement.<ref name="Vote Date" /> In response to the announcement, the 575 employees of [[Chandrila/Legends|Chandrila's]] [[Public Safety Commission]] staged a walk-out in protest of the Act turning over Chandrilan homeland security over to the Republic, resulting in the depersonalization of local services, and the funneling of tax revenues earmarked for local forces to the Army of the Republic.<ref name="Chandrila" />

===The great debate===
{{Quote|There are many on both sides of this grand debate eager to turn this dispute into war. It needn't degenerate into so wasteful an outcome. Together, we have the intelligence and the reason to find an alternative solution.|Palpatine, in an open address to Count Dooku|<ref name="Talk" />}}
Seven days after Palpatine's announcement, following a week of closed-door discussions between [[Corellian/Legends|Corellian]] Senator [[Garm Bel Iblis/Legends|Garm Bel Iblis]] and [[Diktat]] [[Shyla Merricope]], Corellia surprised the Republic by announcing that it was invoking its right of ''[[Contemplanys Hermi]]'' and closing its borders. Withdrawing his vote on the Act, Bel Iblis announced that it was a threat to Corellia's sovereignty, and Corellia would not be party to it. Merricope concurred, declaring that Corellians would not be drafted to fight the Republic's wars, nor would they allow the Republic's soldiers to be placed in their homes.<ref name="Corellia" /> The next day, HoloNet News published a "Point/Counterpoint" article on the Act, with [[Judicial/Legends|Judicial]] [[Terrinald Screed/Legends|Terrinald Screed]] endorsing it and [[Caamasi/Legends|Caamasi]] Senator [[Eeshrin Ot'Hyne]] arguing for the opposition.<ref name="Point" />

[[File:Palpatine-HNNVol531-48.png|thumb|right|200px|Palpatine addresses Count Dooku on the HoloNet.]]
Some still continued to push for peace. Chancellor Palpatine made a 12-minute public address on the HoloNet&mdash;overriding almost every channel and feed&mdash;to the secretive Count Dooku, asking for a parley so the two could come to a peaceful solution. Senator [[Onaconda Farr/Legends|Onaconda Farr]] of [[Rodia/Legends|Rodia]] criticized Palpatine for the move, believing it to be a cowardly attempt to stop the Act.<ref name="Talk">{{HoloNetNewsWeb|48|news/13321_1.html|Palpatine to Separatists: Let's Talk}}</ref> On 3:20, Senator [[Horox Ryyder/Legends|Horox Ryyder]] of [[Gravlex Med/Legends|Gravlex Med]], one of those who had campaigned against the Act, retired. His successors [[Zo Howler]] and [[Fo Kuna]] promised to continue his work opposing it.<ref name="Horox Ryyder" /> Palpatine received further criticism from some in the Senate when he revealed the members of the Republic's new [[Loyalist Committee/Legends|Loyalist Committee]]&mdash;an advisory body for dealing with the Separatist Crisis&mdash;on 3:28. Though the committee consisted of Senators on both sides of the Military Creation Act debate, many Senators believed that Palpatine was forming a partisan body to affect the impending vote, with Farr again claiming that the Chancellor was trying to subvert it by gathering his allies.<ref name="Loyalist" />

===Campaigning===
{{Quote|The Academy of Carida has produced some of the finest Planetary Security Forces in the Republic, and was born of the last great military that flew the Republic banner. We aspire to continue that proud tradition, and hone the skills of a grand Army of the Republic, should the Military Creation Act come to pass.|Ambassador Golfhan of Carida|<ref name="Carida" />}}
As the final month before the vote began, the debate continued. On [[Chandrila/Legends|Chandrila]] the [[Legislative Youth Program/Legends|Legislative Youth Program]] held a mock vote on the Act, using a conjectural version of its as-yet-unknown articles. Presided over by [[Junior Chancellor]] [[Kennis Radi]], the mock Senate session included [[Needo Farr]] of Rodia in the support and [[Dashé Borreno]] of [[Naboo/Legends|Naboo]] in the opposition; many delegates could not attend, some because their homes had seceded, some due to fears of travel in the current situation, and in the case of [[Trevor Insevade]] of [[Alderaan/Legends|Alderaan]], due to illness. The Act passed with a margin of 52-48 percent; Borreno believed that Insevade could have turned the vote had he been present.<ref name="Youth" /> In the real Senate, the expected vote tally was even in the last weeks.<ref name="AOTCn" /> Rumors that Palpatine was dealing with health problems, and would take a vacation before the vote, were meanwhile denied by his aide [[Sate Pestage/Legends|Sate Pestage]].<ref name="Health">{{HoloNetNewsWeb|52|news/13418_5.html|Palpatine Health Rumors Denied}}</ref>

On 4:18, the government of [[Carida/Legends|Carida]], home to the longstanding [[Carida Academy/Legends|Academy of Carida]], joined the campaigning for the Act, donating billions of credits towards regional campaigning efforts and offering the Academy for Republic use in training its new army, if the Act passed. [[Ambassador/Legends|Ambassador]] [[Golfhan]] of Carida vowed to continue the military traditions of the Republic that had given rise to the Academy. The move was met with praise by some, including Terrinald Screed, but others like Senator [[Padmé Amidala/Legends|Padmé Amidala]] of [[Naboo/Legends|Naboo]]&mdash;campaigning against the Act in her native [[Chommell sector/Legends|Chommell sector]] at the time&mdash;saw it as a bid solely to promote the interests of the Academy.<ref name="Carida" />

[[File:SenateGuards.jpg|thumb|left|180px|Senate Guards break up a protest outside the Senate Rotunda.]]
Senator Farr, meanwhile, aided in his side of the campaigning by bankrolling and writing the story of a play that was also a political message: ''[[The Trickery of Vosdia Nooma]]'', produced by the Rodian government's [[Drama Council]]. Laden with allegory and symbolism, the play promoted Farr's pro-military positions and a pro-Military Creation Act stance in particular. Farr himself had a cameo in the play, though drama editor [[Korvit Domesa]] of HoloNet News, who reviewed the play, believed this was a mistake that could hurt his platform; Domesa nonetheless thought that the production would inspire discussion on both sides of the debate.<ref name="Rodian">{{HoloNetNewsWeb|52|life/13418_2.html|Rodian Campaigning Mixes Drama & Politics}}</ref> But all interactions were not peaceful; in the weeks leading up to the vote, the number of vocal opponents and supporters rose outside the [[Grand Convocation Chamber|Senate Rotunda]] on Coruscant. Approximately 7,000 activists gathered around the building, most in protest; a number of isolated fights broke out between them and the smaller&mdash;but still vocal&mdash;group of pro-Act demonstrators. On 5:9 the [[Senate Guard/Legends|Senate Guard]] attempted to relocate the crowds. When the protesters pushed back, violence broke out, and the guards fired stun blasts into the crowd. Thirty-eight individuals were arrested, many of them students from the [[University of Coruscant/Legends|University of Coruscant]], and four activists and two guards had to be rushed to the hospital.<ref name="Rally">{{HoloNetNewsWeb|55|news/1359_1.html|Anti-War Rally Dispersed by Senate Guard}}</ref>

As the vote neared, Senators and representatives began their final tallies of the consensus of their constituents. The [[Mid Rim/Legends|Mid Rim]] in particular filled with campaigning as every sector tried to make its voice heard. Though each Senate vote was decided by the local custom of the sector, most used some sort of referendum to hear the will of their constituency. Senator Amidala continued her efforts against the Act in the Chommell sector, while Senator [[Yudrish Sedran/Legends|Yudrish Sedran]] of [[Chalacta/Legends|Chalacta]] came out against it as well after consulting with the [[Chalactan/Legends|Chalactan]] [[Temple of Illumination]], a decision that was supported by Chalactan Jedi [[Depa Billaba/Legends|Depa Billaba]] and [[Sar Labooda/Legends|Sar Labooda]]. Meanwhile, Senator [[Jollin Resbin]] of [[Sneeve/Legends|Sneeve]], a supporter of the Act, gained the endorsement of retired [[Podracing/Legends|podracing]] champion [[Boles Roor/Legends|Boles Roor]], who not only appeared in advertisements for Resbin, but even came out of retirement to participate in a series of charity races around the Mid Rim to spread the Senator's message. However, political analysts agreed that it would ultimately be the say of the [[Core Worlds/Legends|Core Worlds]] that decided the vote. With seven days left until the vote, many Senators began returning to Coruscant.<ref name="Mid Rim" />

The night before the vote, 5:15, Palpatine made an address to the Republic announcing his confidence in negotiations towards a peaceful sentiment, regardless of whether the Act passed; his words were perceived by the media as acceptance of a likely "yes" vote.<ref name="Confident">{{HoloNetNewsWeb|56|news/13516_4.html|Palpatine Confident in Negotiations}}</ref>

===Assassination attempt and the Grand Army of the Republic===
{{Quote|I have led the opposition to building this army, and someone will stop at nothing to assure its passage.|Senator Padmé Amidala, after her assassination attempt|<ref name="Alive" />}}
5:16, the day of the vote, came at last. Senator Amidala was amongst those returning to Coruscant, and with many knowing that fact and not wanting her to cast her vote, she was under heavy protection.<ref name="AOTCn" /> As her [[J-type diplomatic barge/Legends|starship]] landed on one of Coruscant's platforms and her decoy [[Cordé/Legends|Cordé]] disembarked, a bomb [[Plot to assassinate Senator Amidala/Legends|detonated]], killing Cordé but leaving Amidala alive. The would-be [[Assassin/Legends|assassin]] was [[Zam Wesell/Legends|Zam Wesell]], a [[Bounty hunter/Legends|bounty hunter]] hired by [[Jango Fett/Legends|Jango Fett]], in turn an employee of Count Dooku.<ref name="AOTC" /> Amidala was presumed dead, and HoloNet News even published an obituary shortly thereafter.<ref name="Alive" />

[[File:Padme_Military_Act.png|thumb|right|220px|Padmé Amidala speaks after her presumed assassination.]]
As these events were occurring, the Act was at last coming to a vote in the Senate, intended to be decided by 0800.<ref name="Alive" /> The recent demonstrations around the Senate and general atmosphere of fear had driven the Senators into an uproar, but they were soon silenced when Palpatine announced that Amidala had been assassinated. Even this news would not stop the call for a vote, however, and [[Ask Aak/Legends|Ask Aak]] of Malastare declared that Amidala's death was further proof of the need for an army. Palpatine urged the Senate to push for peace and a storm of arguments again rose, but the Senate was silenced for a second time when Amidala herself appeared. After concurring with the Chancellor's plea for peace, the Senator made an announcement to the surprised body of legislators, announcing her suspicion that one of her political enemies had been behind the attempt to kill her. Amidst another round of argument, Senator [[Orn Free Taa/Legends|Orn Free Taa]] moved that the vote be deferred,<ref name="AOTCn" /> and Palpatine adjourned the Senate and delayed the vote until a later session the following day. The pro-military faction soon claimed that Palpatine had overstepped his authority in the delay, with Senator [[Candabrine Bu]] of [[Lansono]] doubting that the Chancellor had ever intended the vote to be held that day.<ref name="Alive" /> Palpatine meanwhile conferred with the Jedi Order, expressing his desire to hold off the vote and his fear that it would tear the Republic apart.<ref name="AOTCn" />

Palpatine had other motives, though, as he secretly wanted the measure passed. To remove Amidala and her vote from the Senate, he assigned the Jedi [[Obi-Wan Kenobi/Legends|Obi-Wan Kenobi]] to protect her, knowing full well that his apprentice, [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Anakin Skywalker]]&mdash;who he knew harbored feelings for the Senator<ref name="DL">''[[Dark Lord: The Rise of Darth Vader]]''</ref>&mdash; would be present with him, to protect her, and after another assassination attempt on Amidala's life that night, the Chancellor ordered her to go into hiding with Skywalker on Naboo. Though upset that she would not be on Coruscant to spearhead the opposition to the Act, Amidala complied. Meanwhile, Skywalker's master [[Obi-Wan Kenobi/Legends|Obi-Wan Kenobi]], in the process of investigating the assassinations, discovered a [[Clone trooper/Legends|clone army]] on the world of [[Kamino/Legends|Kamino]], commissioned by the long-dead [[Jedi Master/Legends|Jedi Master]] [[Sifo-Dyas/Legends|Sifo-Dyas]]. Kenobi soon came across evidence that the Separatists had developed an army of their own and were preparing to use it against the Republic.<ref name="AOTC" /> With the Senate still deadlocked over the issue of the army, the Loyalist Committee, heads of the Jedi Order, and Chancellor Palpatine decided on a new tactic. [[Junior Representative/Legends|Representative]] [[Jar Jar Binks/Legends|Jar Jar Binks]], standing in for Amidala while she was away, would call for emergency powers to be invested in the Chancellor, allowing him to activate the clone army. With Amidala's noted anti-military stance, the support of Binks, as her proxy, would draw over many of the others on her side. It was successful; Palpatine was granted the powers, activating the clones to form a [[Grand Army of the Republic/Legends|Grand Army of the Republic]]. The [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]] began with their [[First Battle of Geonosis/Legends|first action]] on [[Geonosis/Legends|Geonosis]].<ref name="AOTCn" /> After the outbreak of war, the former opposition to the Act received significant criticism from the pro-military factions, who saw the war as the danger they had sought to protect the Republic from.<ref name="LOE" />

==Controversy==
Senate and public opinion were deeply divided over the issue of the Military Creation Act.<ref name="Vote Date" /> In a [[HoloNet News/Legends|HoloNet News]] poll on the Act, the day after Palpatine's scheduling of the vote, the results were 70% in favor and 30% opposed.<ref name="Quick Poll">{{HoloNetNewsWeb|46||Quick Poll}}</ref> Endorsements came out for both sides, from the public appearances of celebrity podracer Boles Roor for the Act to the quieter opposition of Jedi Depa Billaba and Sar Labooda.<ref name="Mid Rim" /> Advocates of both sides could be extremely vocal, and violence was known to occur between them, with large-scale rioting on the verge of breaking out on Coruscant.<ref name="Rally" />

===Support===
{{Quote|We've wasted enough time while our enemies conspire against us. By year's end, I predict a strong, proud unified army working side by side with the Jedi order to protect our worlds.|Aks Moe|<ref name="Vote Date" />}}
Those who supported the Act, like Republic Judicial Terrinald Screed, believed that the scope of war had gone beyond that which the extant Republic peacekeeping forces, such as sector security or the Jedi, were capable of handling. They pointed to the inefficiencies of the Stark Hyperspace War as an example of the necessity of a unified military. With sectors and worlds seceding, local forces could not be indefinitely relied on to support the Republic, and private armies, many consisting of droids that were both cheap and numerous, were more common. If the Separatist forces were to consolidate an army, an army would be needed to oppose them; the victory of the [[Gungan/Legends|Gungans]] over the [[Trade Federation/Legends|Trade Federation]] in the [[Invasion of Naboo/Legends|Invasion of Naboo]] ten years prior was pointed to as an example of the value of keeping a standing military in peacetime.<ref name="Point" /> Screed also saw support of the Act as a matter of loyalty, and along with Ambassador Golfhan of Carida, whose government donated billions of credits towards campaigning efforts for the Act, appealed to the military tradition of the Republic as a source of pride.<ref name="Carida" />

Some Senators, like Onaconda Farr, thought war was inevitable.<ref name="Talk" /> Farr's Rodian culture, as well, gave him a long tradition of militarism that drove him to support the Republic's efforts towards an army.<ref name="Split" /> Senator [[Aks Moe/Legends|Aks Moe]] of [[Malastare/Legends|Malastare]] believed the lack of an army gave the Separatists time to conspire against the Republic, and Senator Tikkes worried that at the rates of secession there would be no worlds left in the Republic by the time it got an army.<ref name="Vote Date" /> In the brief time that Senator Amidala was believed to be dead, her presumed assassination provided further proof for the Act's supporters that an army was needed. Other supporters included [[Darsana/Legends|Darsana]] of [[Glee Anselm/Legends|Glee Anselm]];<ref name="AOTCn" /> Jollin Resbin of Sneeve;<ref name="Mid Rim" /> Candabrine Bu of Lansono;<ref name="Alive" /> [[Ask Aak/Legends|Ask Aak]] of Malastare, a longtime proponent of greater military force and a critic of the Jedi; and [[Ronet Coorr]] of [[Iseno/Legends|Iseno]], whose homeworld had a long history of military presence. Two were more uncertain: [[Orn Free Taa/Legends|Orn Free Taa]], who was expected to vote for the army but against any spending increases that came out of his budgets; and [[Bail Prestor Organa/Legends|Bail Organa]] of [[Alderaan/Legends|Alderaan]], who despite not being a strong militarist had spent the last years calling for action against the Separatists.<ref name="Split" />

===Opposition===
{{Quote|Wake up, Senators&mdash;you must wake up! If we offer the Separatists violence, they can only show us violence in return! Many will lose their lives, and all will lose their freedom.|Padmé Amidala, speaking to the Galactic Senate|<ref name="AOTCn" />}}
A wide variety of arguments existed against the Act. Some, like Senator [[Tendau Bendon/Legends|Tendau Bendon]] of [[Ithor/Legends|Ithor]], argued that authorizing a military would provoke the Separatists into war.<ref name="Vote Date" /> Caamasi Senator Eeshrin Ot'Hyne took this view as well, arguing that the pro-army stance was rooted in fear and that rather than being a solution to that fear, a military would only increase violence, a cycle that he said occurred many times throughout the Republic's history. Ot'Hyne beseeched the Republic to address the causes that would lead to a war, saying this would prevent war itself.<ref name="Point" /> Senator Padmé Amidala&mdash;a particularly vocal opponent of the Act who, despite having campaigned against the Act since its announcement, nonetheless left her vote to the choice of her constituency&mdash;<ref name="Mid Rim" />believed it would be a threat to the [[Galactic Constitution/Legends|Galactic Constitution]].<ref name="LOE" /> Amidala headed the [[Campaign against Republic Militarization]],<ref name="Alive" /> which received a share of controversy.<ref name="Stark">{{HoloNetNewsWeb|45|news/13228_4.html|Stark Veterans Blast Amidala}}</ref> Amidala's strong opposition to the measure would, ultimately, be what led to the creation of an army; the trust she earned among the rest of the opposition provided the political capital that her proxy, Representative Binks, needed to reverse her position and grant emergency powers to Chancellor Palpatine.<ref name="AOTCn" />

[[File:YoungBelIblis.jpg|thumb|left|180px|Garm Bel Iblis exits the Galactic Senate chambers after invoking ''Contemplanys Hermi''.]]
Pragmatic arguments existed as well. Chandrilans working in public safety, like [[Ocandra Leeds]], argued that taxes reserved for local forces would have to be transferred to the Republic, depersonalizing the services they offered.<ref name="Chandrila" /> The [[Aqualish/Legends|Aqualish]] of Ando saw it as an insult, as the Republic had many times before ordered them to demilitarize.<ref name="Ando" /> Ot'Hyne suggested that the military funds would be better spent on the [[Diplomatic Corps]] and [[Refugee Relief Movement/Legends|Refugee Relief Movement]], and he declared that commercial interests wanted to capitalize on the conflict for their own ends.<ref name="Point" /> Senator Garm Bel Iblis of Corellia, meanwhile, argued that the costs of the Army would be great, and would all come from Republic taxpayers; planetary security forces, he stated, had worked and would continue to work, and worlds like his own would not want to pay for both an Army of the Republic and their own forces.<ref name="Vote Date" /> Bel Iblis also believed that the Act threatened Corellia's sovereignty, and the Diktat of Corellia did not wish for Corellians to fight and die for the Republic, far from their home planet, nor for soldiers to be billeted in Corellian homes.<ref name="Corellia" />

While the pro-Act movement had several large special interests providing funding, the opposition did not have any donors nearly as sizable.<ref name="Carida" /> In the final month before the vote, a number of students from the University of Coruscant protested the Act in front of the Senate Rotunda.<ref name="Rally" /> Other opponents included Horox Ryyder, Zo Howler, and Fo Kuna of Gravlex Med,<ref name="Horox Ryyder" /> Yudrish Sedran of Chalacta,<ref name="Mid Rim" /> [[Mon Mothma/Legends|Mon Mothma]] of [[Chandrila/Legends|Chandrila]], [[Fang Zar/Legends|Fang Zar]] of [[Sern Prime/Legends|Sern Prime]],<ref name="ROTSVD">''[[Star Wars: Revenge of the Sith: The Visual Dictionary]]''</ref> and [[Lexi Dio/Legends|Lexi Dio]] of the peaceful and independent [[Agriworld/Legends|agriworld]] [[Uyter/Legends|Uyter]].<ref name="Split" /> Supreme Chancellor Palpatine himself publicly stated he opposed the Act, though in several announcements he remained nonpartisan on the issue;<ref name="Vote Date" /> some Senators, however, believed many of his political actions were attempts to undermine it.<ref name="Talk" /><ref name="Loyalist" /> In secret, Palpatine sought to pass the Act, even attempting to remove influential votes against it like those of Senator Amidala.<ref name="DL" />

==Behind the scenes==
Created as a major element for the plot of [[Star Wars: Episode II Attack of the Clones|''Star Wars'': Episode II ''Attack of the Clones'']], the Military Creation Act was introduced in [[HoloNet News (original website)|HoloNet News]], a regular online feature preceding the release of ''Attack of the Clones''. The Act, and the circumstances surrounding it, formed a running narrative throughout HoloNet News up until the movie's release.
